chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Musa al-Hannat narrated to me; he said:
I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who drinks wine and then spits it out from his mouth, and it reaches my garment. He said: “There is no harm.”

That which indicates that these reports are to be understood as issued under taqiyyah is what was previously mentioned from the verse, and that Allah, Exalted is He, applied the name of filth to wine. It is not permissible that there should issue from their side that which contradicts the Qur'an and opposes it. Also, we have already cited reports that oppose these, and reconciliation between them is not possible except by carrying these upon taqiyyah, because if we were to act upon these reports, we would be setting aside the rulings of those others altogether and would not be taking them in any way. But if we act upon those reports, we would be acting in accordance with what agrees with the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. So we carried these upon taqiyyah, because taqiyyah is one of the aspects for whose sake reports may validly issue from them, and thus we would be acting upon all of them in a way in which there is no contradiction. What also indicates that these reports were issued by way of taqiyyah is the following.

No. (826) 113 — What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abu al-Qasim Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yaʿqub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmir, from ʿAli ibn Mahziyar; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ʿAli; and ʿAli ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from ʿAli ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I read in the letter of ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, Zurarah narrated from Abi Jaʿfar and Abi ʿAbd Allah عليهما السلام concerning wine that comes upon a man’s garment, that they both said: ‘There is no harm in praying in it; only drinking it was forbidden.’ And someone other than Zurarah narrated from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام that he said: ‘If wine or nabidh — meaning the intoxicant — reaches your garment, then wash it, if you know its place; and if you do not know its place, then wash all of it; and if you prayed in it, then repeat your salat (prayer).’ So inform me what I should take by.” Then he wrote in his own hand, عليه السلام: “And I have read it. Take by the statement of Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام.”

The manner of inference from the report is that he عليه السلام commanded taking the statement of Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام alone, and turning away from his statement together with the statement of Abi Jaʿfar عليه السلام. Were it not that his statement عليه السلام together with the statement of Abi Jaʿfar عليه السلام had issued in the manner of taqiyyah, then taking both of their statements عليهما السلام together would have been more proper and more fitting. Moreover, the reports we cited last do not state that there is no harm in praying in garments affected by wine; rather, he was only asked about a garment touched by wine and he said: there is no harm in it. It is possible that this means the negation of prohibition regarding wearing it and benefiting from it, even if prayer in it is not permissible.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: taqiyyah; dissimulation or precaution under which some reports are understood to have been issued
key_terms.الرِّجَاسَةِ: filth or impurity; the designation applied to wine in the argument
key_terms.النَّبِيذُ: nabidh; here specified as the intoxicating beverage
key_terms.الِاسْتِدْلَالِ: inference; the legal reasoning drawn from the report
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: wine; the intoxicating substance discussed as affecting garments
key_terms.ثَوْبِي: my garment; the clothing affected by the wine
key_terms.صَلَاتَكَ: your salat (prayer); the prayer to be repeated if performed in the affected garment
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: then wash it; the command regarding a garment reached by wine or intoxicating nabidh

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith reconcile conflicting reports about wine on clothing and prayer in such garments?
ai.summary: This passage discusses reports about wine contacting clothing and the method of reconciling apparently conflicting hadith. It presents the ruling to wash garments affected by intoxicants and explains that contrary reports are understood as having been issued under taqiyyah so that the narrations remain consistent with the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.
